concepts.definition: A statement of the specific benefit a defined customer gets and why it is better for them than the alternatives.
Reeves's requirement of a specific, unique and strong proposition to the buyer.
The change in the user's life that a product benefit leads to.
Evidence that makes a promise believable, from demonstrations to guarantees.

questions.q: Use the "so what?" technique on the feature "30 lessons".
questions.a: For example: so you learn at your own pace; so you can fit learning into lunch breaks; so you finish without taking time off.

questions.q: Why is "do nothing" often the main competitor?
questions.a: Many buyers can live with the problem, so the copy must show the cost of the status quo.

questions.q: Which is more credible for an unknown brand, a guarantee or customer testimonials, and why?
questions.a: Both help; a demonstration the reader can check is strongest, testimonials show others had results, and a guarantee shifts risk without proving the claim.
